A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Deepa Subramanian, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?
options: The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member must obtain a valid Certificate of Practice granted by the Council, which must be renewed annually in accordance with prescribed regulations.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?
options: Whenever the member fails to attend three consecutive Annual General Meetings of the Institute without obtaining prior written leave of absence.
Whenever the member's calculated actuarial reserves for a client are challenged or modified during a routine statutory financial audit.
If the member changes their primary employment from a life insurance company to a non-actuarial commercial software development company.
If the member is deceased, defaults on annual subscription fees, is declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or is convicted of moral turpitude.
explanationCorrect: Section 11 mandates removal for death, request, default in fees, unsound mind by a court, undischarged insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, or disciplinary expulsion.
explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?
options: A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.
A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
explanationCorrect: Section 12 specifies that Council shall consist of not more than 16 members, including at least 9 elected members, up to 4 Central Government nominees, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 14 (Duration and Term of Council)
question: Under Section 14 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the statutory duration of the term of office for the Council of the Institute?
options: The Council holds office permanently until dissolved by an executive notification issued by the Insurance Regulatory Authority.
The Council holds office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution, subject to statutory dissolution provisions.
The Council holds office for a term of five years concurrent with the term of the Lok Sabha of the Parliament of India.
The Council holds office for a term of two years, with half of the elected members retiring annually through rotational ballot.
explanationCorrect: Section 14(1) establishes that the Council shall hold office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution.
explanationIncorrect: The term of Council under the Actuaries Act 2006 is three years, not five years, two years, or permanent.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?
options: Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.
Nominated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India from among senior Appointed Actuaries serving in the industry.
Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Appointed directly by the Minister of Finance from a panel of senior Fellows submitted by the outgoing President of the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 17, the Council elects a President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary from among its elected members for a one-year term.
explanationIncorrect: Office bearers are elected by Council from among its elected members, not appointed by the Finance Minister, IRDAI, or student vote.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?

A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.

explanationIncorrect: The statutory penalty under Section 38 is fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000 on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?

The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.

explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?

Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?

Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 17, the Council elects a President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary from among its elected members for a one-year term.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?
options: A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.
explanationIncorrect: Offences are tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class on complaint by Council or Central Govt under Section 41.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)
question: Under Section 56 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the mandatory statutory condition that the Council must satisfy before making or amending Regulations under the Act?
options: The Regulations require the prior written concurrence of the Chairperson of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.
The Regulations must be ratified by a two-thirds majority vote of all registered student and Associate members at an extraordinary general meeting.
The Council must obtain the prior approval of the Central Government and publish the Regulations in the Official Gazette of India.
The Council can enact Regulations autonomously by a simple majority vote of elected members without any external governmental review.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 56, Regulations made by the Council require the prior approval of the Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.
explanationIncorrect: Section 56 strictly requires the prior approval of the Central Government for Council Regulations. Council cannot enact them autonomously.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the legislative enactment, Presidential assent, and territorial commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006 is legally accurate?
options: It is a delegated administrative regulation issued directly by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority under the Insurance Act 1938 applying to appointed actuaries.
It was originally enacted in 1944 as a colonial British ordinance and was extensively amended in 2006 to incorporate general insurance reserving practitioners.
It is Act No. 42 of 2008 passed by Parliament, took effect on 1 January 2009, and applies exclusively to commercial financial corporations in Mumbai.
It is Act No. 35 of 2006, received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
explanationCorrect: The Actuaries Act 2006 is Act No. 35 of 2006. It received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
explanationIncorrect: The Act is primary Central parliamentary legislation enacted in 2006, not an IRDAI circular, colonial code, or state ordinance.

question: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the precise statutory definition of an 'Actuary'?
options: A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
A corporate finance officer or certified risk manager authorized by a life insurance board of directors to sign quarterly financial statements.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Amit Trivedi, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?

The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?

If the member is deceased, defaults on annual subscription fees, is declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or is convicted of moral turpitude.

explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?

A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
explanationCorrect: Section 12 specifies that Council shall consist of not more than 16 members, including at least 9 elected members, up to 4 Central Government nominees, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Suresh Iyer, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?
options: The member must obtain a valid Certificate of Practice granted by the Council, which must be renewed annually in accordance with prescribed regulations.
The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?
options: Whenever the member's calculated actuarial reserves for a client are challenged or modified during a routine statutory financial audit.
If the member is deceased, defaults on annual subscription fees, is declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or is convicted of moral turpitude.
Whenever the member fails to attend three consecutive Annual General Meetings of the Institute without obtaining prior written leave of absence.
If the member changes their primary employment from a life insurance company to a non-actuarial commercial software development company.
explanationCorrect: Section 11 mandates removal for death, request, default in fees, unsound mind by a court, undischarged insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, or disciplinary expulsion.
explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?
options: Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
explanationCorrect: Section 12 specifies that Council shall consist of not more than 16 members, including at least 9 elected members, up to 4 Central Government nominees, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 14 (Duration and Term of Council)
question: Under Section 14 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the statutory duration of the term of office for the Council of the Institute?
options: The Council holds office permanently until dissolved by an executive notification issued by the Insurance Regulatory Authority.
The Council holds office for a term of five years concurrent with the term of the Lok Sabha of the Parliament of India.
The Council holds office for a term of two years, with half of the elected members retiring annually through rotational ballot.
The Council holds office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution, subject to statutory dissolution provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 14(1) establishes that the Council shall hold office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution.
explanationIncorrect: The term of Council under the Actuaries Act 2006 is three years, not five years, two years, or permanent.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?
options: Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Appointed directly by the Minister of Finance from a panel of senior Fellows submitted by the outgoing President of the Institute.
Nominated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India from among senior Appointed Actuaries serving in the industry.
Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 17, the Council elects a President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary from among its elected members for a one-year term.
explanationIncorrect: Office bearers are elected by Council from among its elected members, not appointed by the Finance Minister, IRDAI, or student vote.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory penalty under Section 38 is fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000 on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?
options: The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.
explanationIncorrect: Offences are tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class on complaint by Council or Central Govt under Section 41.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)
question: Under Section 56 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the mandatory statutory condition that the Council must satisfy before making or amending Regulations under the Act?

explanationCorrect: Under Section 56, Regulations made by the Council require the prior approval of the Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.
explanationIncorrect: Section 56 strictly requires the prior approval of the Central Government for Council Regulations. Council cannot enact them autonomously.

question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?

question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?
options: A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)

question: Which of the following statements regarding the legislative enactment, Presidential assent, and territorial commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006 is legally accurate?

It is Act No. 35 of 2006, received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.

explanationIncorrect: The Act is primary Central parliamentary legislation enacted in 2006, not an IRDAI circular, colonial code, or state ordinance.

question: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the precise statutory definition of an 'Actuary'?
options: Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
A corporate finance officer or certified risk manager authorized by a life insurance board of directors to sign quarterly financial statements.
A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?

The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Priya Venkat, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?

A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Ananya Sengupta, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?
options: The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
The member must obtain a valid Certificate of Practice granted by the Council, which must be renewed annually in accordance with prescribed regulations.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?
options: Whenever the member's calculated actuarial reserves for a client are challenged or modified during a routine statutory financial audit.
Whenever the member fails to attend three consecutive Annual General Meetings of the Institute without obtaining prior written leave of absence.
If the member changes their primary employment from a life insurance company to a non-actuarial commercial software development company.
If the member is deceased, defaults on annual subscription fees, is declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or is convicted of moral turpitude.
explanationCorrect: Section 11 mandates removal for death, request, default in fees, unsound mind by a court, undischarged insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, or disciplinary expulsion.
explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?
options: A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.
A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
explanationCorrect: Section 12 specifies that Council shall consist of not more than 16 members, including at least 9 elected members, up to 4 Central Government nominees, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 14 (Duration and Term of Council)
question: Under Section 14 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the statutory duration of the term of office for the Council of the Institute?
options: The Council holds office permanently until dissolved by an executive notification issued by the Insurance Regulatory Authority.
The Council holds office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution, subject to statutory dissolution provisions.
The Council holds office for a term of two years, with half of the elected members retiring annually through rotational ballot.
The Council holds office for a term of five years concurrent with the term of the Lok Sabha of the Parliament of India.
explanationCorrect: Section 14(1) establishes that the Council shall hold office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution.
explanationIncorrect: The term of Council under the Actuaries Act 2006 is three years, not five years, two years, or permanent.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?
options: Nominated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India from among senior Appointed Actuaries serving in the industry.
Appointed directly by the Minister of Finance from a panel of senior Fellows submitted by the outgoing President of the Institute.
Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 17, the Council elects a President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary from among its elected members for a one-year term.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?

explanationIncorrect: The statutory penalty under Section 38 is fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000 on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?

A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.

A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.

Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?

Appointed directly by the Minister of Finance from a panel of senior Fellows submitted by the outgoing President of the Institute.
Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?
options: A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.
explanationIncorrect: Offences are tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class on complaint by Council or Central Govt under Section 41.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)
question: Under Section 56 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the mandatory statutory condition that the Council must satisfy before making or amending Regulations under the Act?
options: The Council can enact Regulations autonomously by a simple majority vote of elected members without any external governmental review.
The Regulations require the prior written concurrence of the Chairperson of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.
The Council must obtain the prior approval of the Central Government and publish the Regulations in the Official Gazette of India.
The Regulations must be ratified by a two-thirds majority vote of all registered student and Associate members at an extraordinary general meeting.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 56, Regulations made by the Council require the prior approval of the Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.
explanationIncorrect: Section 56 strictly requires the prior approval of the Central Government for Council Regulations. Council cannot enact them autonomously.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the legislative enactment, Presidential assent, and territorial commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006 is legally accurate?
options: It is Act No. 42 of 2008 passed by Parliament, took effect on 1 January 2009, and applies exclusively to commercial financial corporations in Mumbai.
It is a delegated administrative regulation issued directly by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority under the Insurance Act 1938 applying to appointed actuaries.
It was originally enacted in 1944 as a colonial British ordinance and was extensively amended in 2006 to incorporate general insurance reserving practitioners.
It is Act No. 35 of 2006, received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
explanationCorrect: The Actuaries Act 2006 is Act No. 35 of 2006. It received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
explanationIncorrect: The Act is primary Central parliamentary legislation enacted in 2006, not an IRDAI circular, colonial code, or state ordinance.

question: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the precise statutory definition of an 'Actuary'?
options: A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
A corporate finance officer or certified risk manager authorized by a life insurance board of directors to sign quarterly financial statements.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Rohan Mehta, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?

The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?

explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?

Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.
A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.

explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.
