A corporate finance officer or certified risk manager authorized by a life insurance board of directors to sign quarterly financial statements.
Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Amit Trivedi, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?
options: The member must obtain a valid Certificate of Practice granted by the Council, which must be renewed annually in accordance with prescribed regulations.
The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?
options: If the member changes their primary employment from a life insurance company to a non-actuarial commercial software development company.
If the member is deceased, defaults on annual subscription fees, is declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or is convicted of moral turpitude.
Whenever the member's calculated actuarial reserves for a client are challenged or modified during a routine statutory financial audit.
Whenever the member fails to attend three consecutive Annual General Meetings of the Institute without obtaining prior written leave of absence.
explanationCorrect: Section 11 mandates removal for death, request, default in fees, unsound mind by a court, undischarged insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, or disciplinary expulsion.
explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?
options: Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.
A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
A maximum of 16 members, comprising a minimum of 9 elected by Fellows and Associates, up to 4 nominated by Central Government, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
explanationCorrect: Section 12 specifies that Council shall consist of not more than 16 members, including at least 9 elected members, up to 4 Central Government nominees, and up to 3 nominated/ex-officio.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 14 (Duration and Term of Council)
question: Under Section 14 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the statutory duration of the term of office for the Council of the Institute?
options: The Council holds office for a term of two years, with half of the elected members retiring annually through rotational ballot.
The Council holds office permanently until dissolved by an executive notification issued by the Insurance Regulatory Authority.
The Council holds office for a term of five years concurrent with the term of the Lok Sabha of the Parliament of India.
The Council holds office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution, subject to statutory dissolution provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 14(1) establishes that the Council shall hold office for a term of three years from the date of its constitution.
explanationIncorrect: The term of Council under the Actuaries Act 2006 is three years, not five years, two years, or permanent.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?
options: Elected annually by the Council from amongst its elected members, holding office for one year and eligible for re-election during their Council term.
Nominated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India from among senior Appointed Actuaries serving in the industry.
Appointed directly by the Minister of Finance from a panel of senior Fellows submitted by the outgoing President of the Institute.
Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 17, the Council elects a President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary from among its elected members for a one-year term.
explanationIncorrect: Office bearers are elected by Council from among its elected members, not appointed by the Finance Minister, IRDAI, or student vote.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 38 (Penalty for Falsely Claiming or Practicing)
question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory penalty under Section 38 is fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000 on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?

A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.
explanationIncorrect: Offences are tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class on complaint by Council or Central Govt under Section 41.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 17 (Election of Office Bearers)
question: Under Section 17 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, how are the President, Vice-President, and Honorary Secretary of the Institute chosen?

Elected directly by a universal postal ballot of all registered student, Associate, and Fellow members of the Institute nationwide.

question: An individual who is not an actuary or does not hold a Certificate of Practice practices actuarial science in India. Under Section 38, what are the statutory criminal penalties?
options: On first conviction, imprisonment up to three years; on subsequent conviction, life imprisonment and forfeiture of all corporate bank accounts.
On first conviction, a fine up to Rs. 1,000; on subsequent conviction, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both.
A mandatory administrative warning notice issued by the Council, with zero monetary fines or criminal prosecution provisions under the Act.
A flat civil penalty of Rs. 10 Lakhs payable directly to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India within fourteen days.
explanationCorrect: Section 38 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 1,000 on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both on subsequent conviction.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 39 (Penalty for Misuse of Name or Awarding Degrees)
question: A private commercial training center in Delhi issues unauthorized certificates awarding the title 'Chartered Actuary of India'. Under Section 39, what statutory penalty applies?
options: The training center is exempt from penalties under Section 39 provided all students execute a disclaimer acknowledging the unofficial status.
A civil penalty of Rs. 25,000 imposed by the Quality Review Board alongside immediate disqualification of all enrolled candidates.
A fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000) for unauthorized use of the Institute's statutory name or awarding misleading designations.
A fine of Rs. 500 per enrolled candidate, payable directly to the Central Government Ministry of Skill Development within thirty days.
explanationCorrect: Section 39 prescribes a fine up to Rs. 10,000 for falsely using the Institute's name, awarding degrees, or misrepresenting actuarial credentials.
explanationIncorrect: Section 39 provides for a criminal fine up to Rs. 10,000, not Rs. 25,000 or exemptions via student disclaimers.

question: Under Section 41 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which court has jurisdiction to try offences under the Act, and upon whose complaint can the court take cognizance?
options: Tried by the independent Quality Review Board sitting as an administrative tribunal without any formal involvement of the judicial magistrate court system.
Tried exclusively by the Supreme Court of India under its original constitutional jurisdiction upon a public interest litigation petition filed by any citizen.
Tried by a local municipal administrative tribunal upon a formal consumer grievance report lodged by an insurance policyholder.
Tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, upon a complaint made by or under order of the Council or Central Government.
explanationCorrect: Section 41 stipulates that no court shall take cognizance except on complaint by Council or Central Govt, tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or JMFC.
explanationIncorrect: Offences are tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class on complaint by Council or Central Govt under Section 41.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 56 (Power to Make Regulations)
question: Under Section 56 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the mandatory statutory condition that the Council must satisfy before making or amending Regulations under the Act?
options: The Council must obtain the prior approval of the Central Government and publish the Regulations in the Official Gazette of India.
The Council can enact Regulations autonomously by a simple majority vote of elected members without any external governmental review.

The Regulations require the prior written concurrence of the Chairperson of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 56, Regulations made by the Council require the prior approval of the Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the legislative enactment, Presidential assent, and territorial commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006 is legally accurate?
options: It is Act No. 42 of 2008 passed by Parliament, took effect on 1 January 2009, and applies exclusively to commercial financial corporations in Mumbai.
It is Act No. 35 of 2006, received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
It was originally enacted in 1944 as a colonial British ordinance and was extensively amended in 2006 to incorporate general insurance reserving practitioners.
It is a delegated administrative regulation issued directly by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority under the Insurance Act 1938 applying to appointed actuaries.
explanationCorrect: The Actuaries Act 2006 is Act No. 35 of 2006. It received Presidential assent on 27 August 2006, commenced on 10 November 2006, and extends to the whole of India.
explanationIncorrect: The Act is primary Central parliamentary legislation enacted in 2006, not an IRDAI circular, colonial code, or state ordinance.

question: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the precise statutory definition of an 'Actuary'?
options: Any professional mathematician or statistician employed by the Central Government to calculate mortality and population census decrement tables.
A corporate finance officer or certified risk manager authorized by a life insurance board of directors to sign quarterly financial statements.
A person skilled in determining the effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, and who is a Fellow member of the Institute.
Any individual who has completed all Core Principles examinations and is registered as an Associate member with the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 2(1)(a), an 'actuary' means a person skilled in determining present effects of future contingent events or risk analysis, who is a Fellow of the Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Under the statutory definition in the Act, an actuary must be a Fellow member of the Institute; associates, corporate officers, and general statisticians do not qualify.

question: Under Section 2(2) of the Actuaries Act, 2006, when is a member of the Institute deemed to be 'in practice'?
options: Whenever they author an academic research paper or deliver a technical lecture on actuarial modeling at an accredited university.
Only when they are formally designated as the statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company and registered with the IRDAI authority.
Only when they maintain a physical commercial office in Mumbai and employ a minimum staff of five full-time actuarial students.
When, individually or in partnership with actuaries, in consideration of remuneration, they engage in actuarial science or render professional actuarial services.
explanationCorrect: Section 2(2) defines 'being in practice' as engaging in actuarial science, offering to perform actuarial services, or rendering professional advice for remuneration.
explanationIncorrect: Being in practice is triggered by rendering professional services for remuneration, regardless of whether one is an Appointed Actuary or academic lecturer.

question: Under Section 3 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the legal status and corporate structure of the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: A statutory body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the legal capacity to acquire property, sue and be sued in its name.
An unregistered national non-profit charitable trust operating under the direct executive administrative authority of the Ministry of Finance Department of Financial Services.
A subordinate administrative supervisory department of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India operating as a permanent regulatory advisory committee.
A private limited commercial company incorporated under the Companies Act 2013 whose voting shares are held by Indian insurance companies.
explanationCorrect: Section 3 establishes the IAI as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute is an independent statutory body corporate established by Parliament, not a private company, trust, or subordinate IRDAI department.

question: On the commencement of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what statutory consequences occurred regarding the erstwhile Actuarial Society of India (ASI) under Sections 4 and 5?
options: All assets of the ASI were surrendered to the Consolidated Fund of India, and all existing employees were retrenched with statutory compensation.
The ASI was formally dissolved, all assets, debts, and contracts vested in the statutory IAI, and ASI employees became IAI employees on identical terms.
The ASI was merged directly into the Life Insurance Corporation of India to serve as a nationalized training center for life insurance underwriters.
The ASI continued as an independent research society while all regulatory licensing functions were transferred to the newly created Institute.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4 and 5 enacted the dissolution of ASI, the complete transfer and vesting of all assets, debts, and contracts in IAI, and the seamless transfer of all employees.
explanationIncorrect: The ASI was completely dissolved, not merged into LIC or maintained as a parallel entity, and its staff were fully protected as IAI employees.

question: Actuary Meenakshi Sundaram, a Fellow of the Institute, wishes to set up an independent consulting firm to offer statutory valuation services. Under Section 9(1), what mandatory requirement must be satisfied before practicing?
options: The member must deposit a refundable security bond of Rs. 25 Lakhs with the Reserve Bank of India prior to accepting commercial assignments.
The member must obtain an executive operating permit from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and register as a certified chartered accountant.
The member must obtain a valid Certificate of Practice granted by the Council, which must be renewed annually in accordance with prescribed regulations.
The member only needs to hold a valid Fellowship diploma and is exempt from obtaining a separate practice license from the Institute Council.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9(1), no member shall be entitled to practice actuarial science in India without holding a valid annual Certificate of Practice granted by the Council.
explanationIncorrect: Holding a Fellowship diploma alone does not authorize practice; Section 9 makes holding a valid Certificate of Practice mandatory.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Section 11 (Removal from Register of Members)
question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following is a mandatory ground upon which the Council must remove a member's name from the Register?

Whenever the member fails to attend three consecutive Annual General Meetings of the Institute without obtaining prior written leave of absence.

explanationIncorrect: Missing AGMs, changing employment, or having reserves questioned in audit are not grounds for removal from the Register of Members under Section 11.

question: Under Section 12 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, what is the maximum statutory size of the Council and the statutory rule regarding elected members?

A maximum of 10 members, all of whom must be Fellows of the Institute nominated exclusively by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority.
A flexible body of 12 to 20 members, where half the seats are permanently reserved for appointed actuaries of public sector general insurers.
Exactly 25 members, comprising 15 elected Fellows, 5 elected Associates, and 5 external members nominated directly by the President of India.

explanationIncorrect: The statutory cap is 16 members (minimum 9 elected, up to 4 Government nominees). It is not 25 or 10 members.

options: Four sitting judges of the Supreme Court of India nominated directly by the Chief Justice to supervise professional ethics investigations.
Three executive directors of commercial public sector banks appointed on an honorary basis to manage the Institute's cash and treasury reserves.
Shri Debasish Prusty (Notification 11/06/2026), Ms. Girija Subramanian (19/08/2025), and Shri R. Doraiswamy (19/08/2025), representing the Government of India.
Two joint secretaries from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and two regional directors from the Reserve Bank of India serving five-year tenures.
explanationCorrect: Government of India nominees on the IAI Council include Shri Debasish Prusty, Ms. Girija Subramanian, and Shri R. Doraiswamy pursuant to official Gazette notifications.
explanationIncorrect: The Central Government nominees represent public financial governance, not the judiciary, commercial bank treasury departments, or the RBI.

question: Under Section 21 of the Actuaries Act, 2006 and the official IAI governance structure, which of the following is an active Section 21 Standing Committee of the Institute?
options: The National Commercial Tariff Committee, Marine Cargo Pricing Committee, Motor Third Party Rate Setting Board, and Health Insurance Underwriting Guild.
The Private Equity Venture Board, Actuarial Mutual Fund Trust, Stock Market Valuation Committee, and Mergers & Acquisitions Advisory Panel.
The Judicial Execution Committee, Criminal Extradition Directorate, High Court Liaison Bureau, and Civil Penalties Enforcement Department.
The Professionalism Committee, Audit Committee, Finance/HR/IT Committee, Education & Exam Committee, Research Committee, and Student Growth Committee.
explanationCorrect: Active Section 21 Standing Committees include Professionalism, Audit, Finance/HR/IT/Admin, Education & Exam, Research & Innovation, and Student Growth & Success.
explanationIncorrect: Section 21 Committees handle internal governance, professionalism, audit, education, and student growth; commercial pricing or judicial execution bodies do not exist.

source: IAI Governance, Section 21 Committees (Professionalism Committee Role)
question: Under official IAI website governance descriptions, what is the primary role and responsibility of the Section 21 Professionalism Committee?
options: To review PCS interpretations, advise members on ethical dilemmas, monitor compliance with guidance notes, and assess emerging professionalism trends.
To evaluate individual examination scripts for the Specialist Technical examinations and determine student cut-off percentiles.
To audit the daily accounting receipts of the Secretariat, verify vendor travel invoices, and administer employee health insurance policies.
To conduct formal prosecutorial hearings under the Disciplinary Rules 2008 and sentence non-compliant members to custodial imprisonment.
explanationCorrect: The Professionalism Committee acts as the custodian of ethical standards, reviewing PCS interpretations, issuing guidance on ethical dilemmas, and reviewing trends.
explanationIncorrect: Disciplinary prosecution is handled by the Disciplinary Directorate; internal audits by the Audit Committee; exams by the Education & Examination Committee.

question: According to the official Advisory Groups directory on the IAI website, what is the organizational purpose and domain scope of Practice Advisory Groups (PAGs)?
options: Regional social clubs in metropolitan cities that organize recreational sports events and informal networking dinners for actuarial students.
Domain-specific think tanks covering 16 areas including Life, General, Health, Pensions, Risk Management, AI & Data Science, IFRS 17, and Banking.
Statutory appellate courts that hear judicial appeals against decisions rendered by the Quality Review Board and Disciplinary Directorate.
Private commercial partnerships established by Council members to tender for lucrative public sector actuarial consulting contracts.
explanationCorrect: PAGs are specialized technical bodies across 16 areas (Life, GI, Health, Pension, ERM, AI/Data Science, IFRS 17, Banking, Climate Risk, etc.) supporting standard setting and development.
explanationIncorrect: PAGs are domain think-tanks assisting Council on technical standards and research; they are not social clubs, commercial partnerships, or courts.

source: IAI Governance, Advisory Groups (Modern Practice Domains)
question: Reflecting modern actuarial expansion, which of the following contemporary Advisory Groups are officially established under the IAI governance framework?
options: Aviation Claims Litigation, Commercial Space Travel Underwriting, Professional Sports Betting Analytics, and Entertainment Industry Contract Arbitration Boards.
State Electricity Utility Pricing Board, Municipal Water Tariff Council, Highway Toll Concession Panel, and National Telecommunications Spectrum Advisory Bureau.
AI & Data Science, Climate Risk & Sustainable Finance, IFRS 17 (IND AS 117), Actuarial Job Placement (AG-AJP), and Agriculture & Rural Risk Management.
Cryptocurrency Arbitrage, High Frequency Algorithmic Trading Networks, Corporate Tax Evasion Strategies, and Private Offshore Asset Sheltering Structures.
explanationCorrect: Contemporary PAGs on the IAI website include AI & Data Science, Climate Risk & Sustainable Finance, IFRS 17, AG-AJP, and Agriculture & Rural Risk Management.
explanationIncorrect: The Institute's contemporary AGs focus on AI/data science, climate risk, IFRS 17, placements, and agriculture, not cryptocurrency arbitrage or municipal utilities.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Procedure of Conducting AGM - 2 March 2013)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for Conducting Annual General Meetings (approved on 2 March 2013), what is the mandatory notice period required for convening an AGM?
options: Exactly seven calendar days' advance notice transmitted via digital social media channels and published in an English daily newspaper in Mumbai.
A minimum of sixty calendar days' notice accompanied by a full printed copy of all disciplinary inquiry transcripts from the preceding year.
Zero advance notice is required; the President may summon an emergency AGM at two hours' verbal notice by telephone conference call.
A minimum of twenty-one (21) clear days' notice in writing must be given to all members entitled to attend and vote at the Annual General Meeting.
explanationCorrect: Under Council Guidelines for Conducting AGM (approved 2 March 2013), a minimum of 21 clear days' notice in writing is mandatory for convening an AGM.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory and guideline standard for an AGM is 21 clear days' notice in writing to all voting members.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Principles & Procedures for GNs/APSs)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for issuance of Guidance Notes (GNs) and Actuarial Practice Standards (APSs) Versions 3, 4, and 5, what is the standard public consultation window for an Exposure Draft?
options: The Exposure Draft must be published on the IAI website for public consultation and member feedback for a period of thirty (30) to sixty (60) days.
The Exposure Draft must remain open for public comment for a mandatory minimum of twelve months across three consecutive financial years.
The Exposure Draft is circulated confidentially to elected Council members only for forty-eight hours without any public or general member consultation.
Zero public consultation is required; the President can enact an APS immediately as a binding standard upon signing the draft in Council.
explanationCorrect: Under standard setting due process (Versions 3, 4, 5), new APS/GN exposure drafts are published for 30 to 60 days for public and member feedback.
explanationIncorrect: Standard setting due process mandates a 30 to 60 day exposure draft period on the website to ensure broad public and professional consultation.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Social Media Usage & Reputation - Feb 2026)
question: Under the Council Guidelines on 'Use of Social Media and Reputation of the Profession' (dated February 2026), what is the core standard governing members' online conduct?
options: Members may freely publish unverified confidential client valuation results on digital forums provided the post is deleted within twenty-four hours.
Members must uphold professional dignity online and are strictly liable for posts that disparage the Institute, breach confidentiality, or harm professional reputation.
Members are prohibited from maintaining personal profiles on LinkedIn, Twitter, or professional networking platforms under threat of expulsion.
Members are completely immune from disciplinary action for personal social media posts, provided they state 'views expressed are purely personal'.
explanationCorrect: The February 2026 Social Media Guidelines hold members professionally accountable for digital commentary, prohibiting disparagement, confidentiality breaches, and disrepute.
explanationIncorrect: Disclaimers like 'views are personal' do not shield members from disciplinary accountability for unprofessional or defamatory social media conduct.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Advisory on New Labor Codes - 27 Jan 2026)
question: Under the IAI Advisory on the implementation of New Labor Codes for employee benefit valuation (dated 27 January 2026), what guidance is provided to actuaries valuing gratuity liabilities?
options: Actuaries must ignore the New Labor Codes entirely until all state government judicial challenges are definitively settled by the Supreme Court.
Actuaries are forbidden from certifying any employee benefit valuation report until the Ministry of Labour issues company-specific actuarial guidelines.
Actuaries must assess the redefined definition of 'wages' (50% cap on allowances) and evaluate its material financial impact on gratuity and leave encashment reserves.
Actuaries must immediately write off all existing corporate gratuity liabilities and replace them with defined contribution provident fund accounting entries.
explanationCorrect: The 27 Jan 2026 Advisory directs actuaries to evaluate the impact of the amended 'wages' definition (50% allowances rule) on gratuity and employee benefit liabilities.
explanationIncorrect: Actuaries cannot ignore enacted legislation; they must actively model and disclose the impact of the new wage structure on statutory liabilities.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 43 (Quality Review Board)
question: Under Section 43 of the Actuaries Act, 2006 and official IAI governance records, who constitutes the Quality Review Board (QRB) and who serves as its Chairperson?
options: The QRB is constituted by the Council of the Institute, headed by the President of the Institute ex-officio alongside six senior Appointed Actuaries.
The QRB is an informal standing subcommittee of the Professionalism Committee, headed by the Honorary Secretary of the Institute on an annual rotational basis.
The QRB is established by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, headed by the Member (Actuarial) alongside state high court judges.
The QRB is constituted by the Central Government, headed by Chairperson Supratim Bandyopadhyay, alongside four part-time members serving a three-year term.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 43(1), the Central Government constitutes the Quality Review Board, consisting of a Chairperson (Supratim Bandyopadhyay) and 4 members (3-year tenure).
explanationIncorrect: The QRB is appointed by the Central Government under Section 43, not by Council, IRDAI, or the Professionalism Committee.

source: IAI Governance, Quality Review Board - Sec 43 (Composition Breakdown)
question: Under the official governance notifications on the IAI website regarding the Quality Review Board under Section 43, how are the four members of the Board nominated?
options: Two members are nominated by the Central Government and two members are nominated by the Council of the Institute, serving three-year part-time appointments.
All four members are nominated directly by the President of the Institute from among Fellows with twenty years of continuous actuarial practice experience.
Three members are nominated by life insurance companies and one member is nominated by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Four members are elected directly by registered student and Associate members through a nationwide electronic voting ballot conducted every two years.
explanationCorrect: The QRB consists of a Chairperson plus 4 members: 2 nominated by Central Government (Sanjeev Kumar Pujari, G. Ramaswamy) and 2 nominated by Council (Gopal Kumar Vishwanath Roy, Padmaja Raghunathan).
explanationIncorrect: The QRB composition is strictly split: 2 nominated by Central Government and 2 nominated by Council, serving part-time 3-year tenures.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 44 (Functions of QRB)
question: Under Section 44 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following accurately describes the three statutory functions of the Quality Review Board?
options: To manage the annual investments of the Institute's pension funds, negotiate corporate employee salaries, and set registration fees for student examinations.
To fix standards for services provided by members, review quality of services including actuarial audit, and guide members on improving service quality.
To register new insurance companies with the IRDAI, approve life insurance product brochures, and license commercial reinsurance brokers in India.
To conduct disciplinary trials against accused members, impose monetary fines up to Rs. 10 Lakhs, and issue formal reprimands under statutory procedures.
explanationCorrect: Section 44 mandates three functions: (a) fix standards for services, (b) review quality of services including actuarial audit, and (c) guide members on quality and statutory compliance.
explanationIncorrect: The QRB is a quality advisory and review body; it does not conduct disciplinary trials, manage staff salaries, or license insurance companies.

question: Under official IAI website governance records, which statutory rules govern the procedure for meetings, terms of service, and allowances of the Chairperson and Members of the Quality Review Board?
options: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (Appointed Actuary) Regulations 2022 governing corporate governance in public limited insurers.
The Institute of Actuaries of India General Internal Operating By-Laws and Standing Orders enacted by the Executive Director in 2012.
The Actuaries Quality Review Board (Procedure for Meetings, and Terms and Conditions of Service and Allowances of Chairperson and Members) Rules, 2008.
The Civil Procedure Code 1908 governing administrative hearings and commercial arbitrations before the High Court of Judicature at Bombay.
explanationCorrect: The QRB meetings, allowances, and service conditions are governed by the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008 enacted by the Central Government.
explanationIncorrect: The specific governing rules are the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008, not the CPC 1908 or IRDAI Appointed Actuary Regulations.

question: According to the official Council directory on the IAI website, who are the current executive Office Bearers leading the Institute of Actuaries of India?
options: President Kartikey Kandoi, Vice President K S Gopalakrishnan, and Honorary Secretary Pravir Chandra, appointed for five-year non-renewable terms.
A rotating triumvirate of Chief Executive Officers representing the largest three general insurance companies in India serving ex-officio.
President Supratim Bandyopadhyay, Vice President Sanjeev Kumar Pujari, and Honorary Secretary G. Ramaswamy, appointed directly by the Ministry of Finance.
President K S Gopalakrishnan, Vice President Pravir Chandra, and Honorary Secretary Kartikey Kandoi, serving one-year elected terms from among Council members.
explanationCorrect: The current IAI Office Bearers are President K S Gopalakrishnan, Vice President Pravir Chandra, and Honorary Secretary Kartikey Kandoi.
explanationIncorrect: Supratim Bandyopadhyay is Chairperson of QRB. Office Bearers are elected annually by Council from amongst elected members.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Procedure of Conducting AGM - 2 March 2013)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for Conducting Annual General Meetings (approved on 2 March 2013), what is the mandatory notice period required for convening an AGM?
options: A minimum of sixty calendar days' notice accompanied by a full printed copy of all disciplinary inquiry transcripts from the preceding year.
Exactly seven calendar days' advance notice transmitted via digital social media channels and published in an English daily newspaper in Mumbai.

explanationCorrect: Under Council Guidelines for Conducting AGM (approved 2 March 2013), a minimum of 21 clear days' notice in writing is mandatory for convening an AGM.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory and guideline standard for an AGM is 21 clear days' notice in writing to all voting members.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Principles & Procedures for GNs/APSs)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for issuance of Guidance Notes (GNs) and Actuarial Practice Standards (APSs) Versions 3, 4, and 5, what is the standard public consultation window for an Exposure Draft?
options: The Exposure Draft must be published on the IAI website for public consultation and member feedback for a period of thirty (30) to sixty (60) days.
Zero public consultation is required; the President can enact an APS immediately as a binding standard upon signing the draft in Council.
The Exposure Draft must remain open for public comment for a mandatory minimum of twelve months across three consecutive financial years.
The Exposure Draft is circulated confidentially to elected Council members only for forty-eight hours without any public or general member consultation.
explanationCorrect: Under standard setting due process (Versions 3, 4, 5), new APS/GN exposure drafts are published for 30 to 60 days for public and member feedback.
explanationIncorrect: Standard setting due process mandates a 30 to 60 day exposure draft period on the website to ensure broad public and professional consultation.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Social Media Usage & Reputation - Feb 2026)
question: Under the Council Guidelines on 'Use of Social Media and Reputation of the Profession' (dated February 2026), what is the core standard governing members' online conduct?
options: Members are completely immune from disciplinary action for personal social media posts, provided they state 'views expressed are purely personal'.
Members must uphold professional dignity online and are strictly liable for posts that disparage the Institute, breach confidentiality, or harm professional reputation.
Members are prohibited from maintaining personal profiles on LinkedIn, Twitter, or professional networking platforms under threat of expulsion.
Members may freely publish unverified confidential client valuation results on digital forums provided the post is deleted within twenty-four hours.
explanationCorrect: The February 2026 Social Media Guidelines hold members professionally accountable for digital commentary, prohibiting disparagement, confidentiality breaches, and disrepute.
explanationIncorrect: Disclaimers like 'views are personal' do not shield members from disciplinary accountability for unprofessional or defamatory social media conduct.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Advisory on New Labor Codes - 27 Jan 2026)
question: Under the IAI Advisory on the implementation of New Labor Codes for employee benefit valuation (dated 27 January 2026), what guidance is provided to actuaries valuing gratuity liabilities?
options: Actuaries must ignore the New Labor Codes entirely until all state government judicial challenges are definitively settled by the Supreme Court.
Actuaries are forbidden from certifying any employee benefit valuation report until the Ministry of Labour issues company-specific actuarial guidelines.
Actuaries must assess the redefined definition of 'wages' (50% cap on allowances) and evaluate its material financial impact on gratuity and leave encashment reserves.

explanationCorrect: The 27 Jan 2026 Advisory directs actuaries to evaluate the impact of the amended 'wages' definition (50% allowances rule) on gratuity and employee benefit liabilities.
explanationIncorrect: Actuaries cannot ignore enacted legislation; they must actively model and disclose the impact of the new wage structure on statutory liabilities.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 43 (Quality Review Board)
question: Under Section 43 of the Actuaries Act, 2006 and official IAI governance records, who constitutes the Quality Review Board (QRB) and who serves as its Chairperson?

source: IAI Governance, Quality Review Board - Sec 43 (Composition Breakdown)
question: Under the official governance notifications on the IAI website regarding the Quality Review Board under Section 43, how are the four members of the Board nominated?

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 44 (Functions of QRB)
question: Under Section 44 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following accurately describes the three statutory functions of the Quality Review Board?
options: To manage the annual investments of the Institute's pension funds, negotiate corporate employee salaries, and set registration fees for student examinations.

explanationIncorrect: The QRB is a quality advisory and review body; it does not conduct disciplinary trials, manage staff salaries, or license insurance companies.

The Actuaries Quality Review Board (Procedure for Meetings, and Terms and Conditions of Service and Allowances of Chairperson and Members) Rules, 2008.

explanationIncorrect: The specific governing rules are the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008, not the CPC 1908 or IRDAI Appointed Actuary Regulations.

question: Under the Council Guidelines on 'Use of Social Media and Reputation of the Profession' (dated February 2026), what is the core standard governing members' online conduct?
options: Members are completely immune from disciplinary action for personal social media posts, provided they state 'views expressed are purely personal'.
Members may freely publish unverified confidential client valuation results on digital forums provided the post is deleted within twenty-four hours.
Members are prohibited from maintaining personal profiles on LinkedIn, Twitter, or professional networking platforms under threat of expulsion.
Members must uphold professional dignity online and are strictly liable for posts that disparage the Institute, breach confidentiality, or harm professional reputation.
explanationCorrect: The February 2026 Social Media Guidelines hold members professionally accountable for digital commentary, prohibiting disparagement, confidentiality breaches, and disrepute.
explanationIncorrect: Disclaimers like 'views are personal' do not shield members from disciplinary accountability for unprofessional or defamatory social media conduct.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Advisory on New Labor Codes - 27 Jan 2026)
question: Under the IAI Advisory on the implementation of New Labor Codes for employee benefit valuation (dated 27 January 2026), what guidance is provided to actuaries valuing gratuity liabilities?
options: Actuaries must assess the redefined definition of 'wages' (50% cap on allowances) and evaluate its material financial impact on gratuity and leave encashment reserves.
Actuaries are forbidden from certifying any employee benefit valuation report until the Ministry of Labour issues company-specific actuarial guidelines.
Actuaries must ignore the New Labor Codes entirely until all state government judicial challenges are definitively settled by the Supreme Court.
Actuaries must immediately write off all existing corporate gratuity liabilities and replace them with defined contribution provident fund accounting entries.
explanationCorrect: The 27 Jan 2026 Advisory directs actuaries to evaluate the impact of the amended 'wages' definition (50% allowances rule) on gratuity and employee benefit liabilities.
explanationIncorrect: Actuaries cannot ignore enacted legislation; they must actively model and disclose the impact of the new wage structure on statutory liabilities.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 43 (Quality Review Board)
question: Under Section 43 of the Actuaries Act, 2006 and official IAI governance records, who constitutes the Quality Review Board (QRB) and who serves as its Chairperson?
options: The QRB is an informal standing subcommittee of the Professionalism Committee, headed by the Honorary Secretary of the Institute on an annual rotational basis.
The QRB is constituted by the Central Government, headed by Chairperson Supratim Bandyopadhyay, alongside four part-time members serving a three-year term.
The QRB is established by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, headed by the Member (Actuarial) alongside state high court judges.
The QRB is constituted by the Council of the Institute, headed by the President of the Institute ex-officio alongside six senior Appointed Actuaries.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 43(1), the Central Government constitutes the Quality Review Board, consisting of a Chairperson (Supratim Bandyopadhyay) and 4 members (3-year tenure).
explanationIncorrect: The QRB is appointed by the Central Government under Section 43, not by Council, IRDAI, or the Professionalism Committee.

source: IAI Governance, Quality Review Board - Sec 43 (Composition Breakdown)
question: Under the official governance notifications on the IAI website regarding the Quality Review Board under Section 43, how are the four members of the Board nominated?
options: Four members are elected directly by registered student and Associate members through a nationwide electronic voting ballot conducted every two years.
Three members are nominated by life insurance companies and one member is nominated by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 44 (Functions of QRB)
question: Under Section 44 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following accurately describes the three statutory functions of the Quality Review Board?
options: To register new insurance companies with the IRDAI, approve life insurance product brochures, and license commercial reinsurance brokers in India.

explanationIncorrect: The QRB is a quality advisory and review body; it does not conduct disciplinary trials, manage staff salaries, or license insurance companies.

question: Under official IAI website governance records, which statutory rules govern the procedure for meetings, terms of service, and allowances of the Chairperson and Members of the Quality Review Board?

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (Appointed Actuary) Regulations 2022 governing corporate governance in public limited insurers.
The Civil Procedure Code 1908 governing administrative hearings and commercial arbitrations before the High Court of Judicature at Bombay.
The Institute of Actuaries of India General Internal Operating By-Laws and Standing Orders enacted by the Executive Director in 2012.
explanationCorrect: The QRB meetings, allowances, and service conditions are governed by the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008 enacted by the Central Government.
explanationIncorrect: The specific governing rules are the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008, not the CPC 1908 or IRDAI Appointed Actuary Regulations.

question: According to the official Advisory Groups directory on the IAI website, what is the organizational purpose and domain scope of Practice Advisory Groups (PAGs)?

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Procedure of Conducting AGM - 2 March 2013)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for Conducting Annual General Meetings (approved on 2 March 2013), what is the mandatory notice period required for convening an AGM?
options: Zero advance notice is required; the President may summon an emergency AGM at two hours' verbal notice by telephone conference call.
Exactly seven calendar days' advance notice transmitted via digital social media channels and published in an English daily newspaper in Mumbai.
A minimum of sixty calendar days' notice accompanied by a full printed copy of all disciplinary inquiry transcripts from the preceding year.
A minimum of twenty-one (21) clear days' notice in writing must be given to all members entitled to attend and vote at the Annual General Meeting.
explanationCorrect: Under Council Guidelines for Conducting AGM (approved 2 March 2013), a minimum of 21 clear days' notice in writing is mandatory for convening an AGM.
explanationIncorrect: The statutory and guideline standard for an AGM is 21 clear days' notice in writing to all voting members.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Principles & Procedures for GNs/APSs)
question: Under the Council Guidelines for issuance of Guidance Notes (GNs) and Actuarial Practice Standards (APSs) Versions 3, 4, and 5, what is the standard public consultation window for an Exposure Draft?
options: The Exposure Draft must be published on the IAI website for public consultation and member feedback for a period of thirty (30) to sixty (60) days.
The Exposure Draft is circulated confidentially to elected Council members only for forty-eight hours without any public or general member consultation.
Zero public consultation is required; the President can enact an APS immediately as a binding standard upon signing the draft in Council.
The Exposure Draft must remain open for public comment for a mandatory minimum of twelve months across three consecutive financial years.
explanationCorrect: Under standard setting due process (Versions 3, 4, 5), new APS/GN exposure drafts are published for 30 to 60 days for public and member feedback.
explanationIncorrect: Standard setting due process mandates a 30 to 60 day exposure draft period on the website to ensure broad public and professional consultation.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Social Media Usage & Reputation - Feb 2026)
question: Under the Council Guidelines on 'Use of Social Media and Reputation of the Profession' (dated February 2026), what is the core standard governing members' online conduct?
options: Members may freely publish unverified confidential client valuation results on digital forums provided the post is deleted within twenty-four hours.
Members must uphold professional dignity online and are strictly liable for posts that disparage the Institute, breach confidentiality, or harm professional reputation.
Members are prohibited from maintaining personal profiles on LinkedIn, Twitter, or professional networking platforms under threat of expulsion.
Members are completely immune from disciplinary action for personal social media posts, provided they state 'views expressed are purely personal'.
explanationCorrect: The February 2026 Social Media Guidelines hold members professionally accountable for digital commentary, prohibiting disparagement, confidentiality breaches, and disrepute.
explanationIncorrect: Disclaimers like 'views are personal' do not shield members from disciplinary accountability for unprofessional or defamatory social media conduct.

source: IAI Governance, Council Guidelines (Advisory on New Labor Codes - 27 Jan 2026)
question: Under the IAI Advisory on the implementation of New Labor Codes for employee benefit valuation (dated 27 January 2026), what guidance is provided to actuaries valuing gratuity liabilities?
options: Actuaries must immediately write off all existing corporate gratuity liabilities and replace them with defined contribution provident fund accounting entries.
Actuaries must ignore the New Labor Codes entirely until all state government judicial challenges are definitively settled by the Supreme Court.
Actuaries must assess the redefined definition of 'wages' (50% cap on allowances) and evaluate its material financial impact on gratuity and leave encashment reserves.
Actuaries are forbidden from certifying any employee benefit valuation report until the Ministry of Labour issues company-specific actuarial guidelines.
explanationCorrect: The 27 Jan 2026 Advisory directs actuaries to evaluate the impact of the amended 'wages' definition (50% allowances rule) on gratuity and employee benefit liabilities.
explanationIncorrect: Actuaries cannot ignore enacted legislation; they must actively model and disclose the impact of the new wage structure on statutory liabilities.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 43 (Quality Review Board)
question: Under Section 43 of the Actuaries Act, 2006 and official IAI governance records, who constitutes the Quality Review Board (QRB) and who serves as its Chairperson?
options: The QRB is an informal standing subcommittee of the Professionalism Committee, headed by the Honorary Secretary of the Institute on an annual rotational basis.
The QRB is established by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, headed by the Member (Actuarial) alongside state high court judges.
The QRB is constituted by the Council of the Institute, headed by the President of the Institute ex-officio alongside six senior Appointed Actuaries.
The QRB is constituted by the Central Government, headed by Chairperson Supratim Bandyopadhyay, alongside four part-time members serving a three-year term.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 43(1), the Central Government constitutes the Quality Review Board, consisting of a Chairperson (Supratim Bandyopadhyay) and 4 members (3-year tenure).
explanationIncorrect: The QRB is appointed by the Central Government under Section 43, not by Council, IRDAI, or the Professionalism Committee.

source: IAI Governance, Quality Review Board - Sec 43 (Composition Breakdown)
question: Under the official governance notifications on the IAI website regarding the Quality Review Board under Section 43, how are the four members of the Board nominated?
options: Two members are nominated by the Central Government and two members are nominated by the Council of the Institute, serving three-year part-time appointments.
Four members are elected directly by registered student and Associate members through a nationwide electronic voting ballot conducted every two years.
Three members are nominated by life insurance companies and one member is nominated by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
All four members are nominated directly by the President of the Institute from among Fellows with twenty years of continuous actuarial practice experience.
explanationCorrect: The QRB consists of a Chairperson plus 4 members: 2 nominated by Central Government (Sanjeev Kumar Pujari, G. Ramaswamy) and 2 nominated by Council (Gopal Kumar Vishwanath Roy, Padmaja Raghunathan).
explanationIncorrect: The QRB composition is strictly split: 2 nominated by Central Government and 2 nominated by Council, serving part-time 3-year tenures.

source: IAI Governance & Actuaries Act 2006, Section 44 (Functions of QRB)
question: Under Section 44 of the Actuaries Act, 2006, which of the following accurately describes the three statutory functions of the Quality Review Board?
options: To manage the annual investments of the Institute's pension funds, negotiate corporate employee salaries, and set registration fees for student examinations.
To fix standards for services provided by members, review quality of services including actuarial audit, and guide members on improving service quality.
To conduct disciplinary trials against accused members, impose monetary fines up to Rs. 10 Lakhs, and issue formal reprimands under statutory procedures.
To register new insurance companies with the IRDAI, approve life insurance product brochures, and license commercial reinsurance brokers in India.
explanationCorrect: Section 44 mandates three functions: (a) fix standards for services, (b) review quality of services including actuarial audit, and (c) guide members on quality and statutory compliance.
explanationIncorrect: The QRB is a quality advisory and review body; it does not conduct disciplinary trials, manage staff salaries, or license insurance companies.

question: Under official IAI website governance records, which statutory rules govern the procedure for meetings, terms of service, and allowances of the Chairperson and Members of the Quality Review Board?
options: The Civil Procedure Code 1908 governing administrative hearings and commercial arbitrations before the High Court of Judicature at Bombay.
The Institute of Actuaries of India General Internal Operating By-Laws and Standing Orders enacted by the Executive Director in 2012.
The Actuaries Quality Review Board (Procedure for Meetings, and Terms and Conditions of Service and Allowances of Chairperson and Members) Rules, 2008.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (Appointed Actuary) Regulations 2022 governing corporate governance in public limited insurers.
explanationCorrect: The QRB meetings, allowances, and service conditions are governed by the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008 enacted by the Central Government.
explanationIncorrect: The specific governing rules are the Actuaries Quality Review Board Rules, 2008, not the CPC 1908 or IRDAI Appointed Actuary Regulations.

President Supratim Bandyopadhyay, Vice President Sanjeev Kumar Pujari, and Honorary Secretary G. Ramaswamy, appointed directly by the Ministry of Finance.
